hints: Look at what functional group you start with in each case, an ester, a carboxylate salt, and an aldehyde.
Remember that dilute aqueous acid hydrolyses esters and protonates carboxylate ions to give the free acid.
Ask yourself if dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(\text{aq})$ alone can oxidise an aldehyde, or if you need a proper oxidising agent for that change.
walkthrough:
**Identify mixture 1**

Think of this as acid hydrolysis of an ester. Water splits the ester link in acid conditions.

$$\text{RCOOR'} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH}$$

**Apply to mixture 1**

Here the ester is ethyl butanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Hydrolysis gives butanoic acid plus ethanol. So 1 does form a carboxylic acid.

**Identify mixture 2**

This is a carboxylate anion, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-$, plus a strong acid. This is a simple acid-base protonation.

$$\text{RCOO}^- + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{RCOOH}$$

**Apply to mixture 2 and 3**

So 2 gives butanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. Mixture 3 is pentanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$. An aldehyde needs a strong oxidising agent such as acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ to become an acid. Dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(\text{aq})$ alone cannot do this, so 3 gives no carboxylic acid.

**Conclude**

Only 1 and 2 give a carboxylic acid. That matches the combination 1 and 2 only.

options.A: This suggests 1, 2 and 3 all work. Mixtures 1 and 2 are correct, but 3 is wrong because dilute sulfuric acid is not an oxidising agent and will not oxidise pentanal to pentanoic acid.
options.B: This is 1 and 2 only, which is correct. 1 is acid hydrolysis of ethyl butanoate to butanoic acid and ethanol. 2 is protonation of butanoate to butanoic acid. 3 gives no acid.
options.C: This suggests 2 and 3 only. 2 is correct, but 1 is missed and 3 is incorrectly included. Ester hydrolysis in 1 definitely gives an acid, while aldehyde oxidation in 3 needs dichromate, not just dilute acid.
options.D: This suggests 1 only. 1 is correct, but 2 is also correct and is missed. Students choosing this may forget that $\text{RCOO}^- + \text{H}^+$ readily reforms $\text{RCOOH}$.
